method: Every substantive public block was compared against complete Arabic paragraph bodies and relevant local notes, independently of foreign adaptations. Preserve facts, agency, polarity, causal/conditional relations, scope, certainty, qualifications and attributed foundations. Common internal policy remains English evidence, not public copy. No official quotation was model-translated. No external factual update or native-speaker proofreading is claimed. Hash bindings document renewed review requirements; automation does not establish semantic fidelity.

standaloneContextReview.renderContract: Source.vue renders buildReadingIndex().paragraphs[].explanation independently of readingSequence; main prose and coverage rationale cannot rescue an incomplete context. All 245 source explanations retain their own core argument, conditions and attributed premise where present. No repeated foundation suffix is appended.

mainPremisePairs.review: Keep the generational choice between humane and dehumanizing construction; put creation and Incarnation behind an attributed foundations link so the secular entry does not imply that these premises are universally accepted.
Preserve the Church's stated willingness to collaborate with all people in integral development; distinguish this inclusive invitation from its belief that divine action blesses those efforts.

Locate the present letter in the living social-teaching tradition inaugurated by Rerum Novarum; remove the closing invocation while keeping the argument that proclamation cannot ignore concrete social life.
Carry forward technology's possible benefits, harms and uncertain long-term effects; separate the appeal to ask God for wisdom from the practical need to interpret current transformations.

Use Babel as an explicitly biblical interpretation of uniformity and self-assertion, preserving the distinction between coordinated activity and homogenization; do not present the narrative as empirical evidence about AI.

Retain Nehemiah's listening, distributed work and shared responsibility as the narrative's argumentative work; keep his historical prayer in optional biblical context rather than misclassifying the reported action as a prayer addressed to the reader.

Preserve both technology's useful possibilities and its dependence on the choices of designers, funders, regulators and users; relocate the Holy Spirit and biblical construction frame without claiming a morally neutral tool.
Retain the critique of profit that sacrifices the weak and of reducing people to data; explain the two biblical paths as attributed metaphors while preserving plurality as a resource for community.

Retain shared responsibility, the strength-in-weakness biblical premise, differentiated contributors and cooperation between peoples, disciplines and cultures. Arabic does not explicitly name subsidiarity here; explain its cooperative logic without fabricating that term in a quotation.
Use the appeal to remain human amid AI as orientation; keep Jubilee grace and humanity revealed in Christ as foundations rather than treating the ceremony as the source's main policy proposal.
Retain the call to plan, work and center people ordinarily excluded, while removing the direct prayer and implored blessing clauses; the common-good task must survive those exclusions.

Retain lay faithful and all people of good will applying principles in daily life, family, work and participation; academics and universities renewing them for digital change; theological/philosophical support for pastoral and teaching work.

Keep four locally named meanings separate: moral الكرامة الأخلاقيّة, social الكرامة الاجتماعيّة, experienced كرامة الحياة, intrinsic الكرامة الوجوديّة. The first three vary; no sin, failure, humiliation or exclusion removes the last, grounded here in divine willing, creation and love.

Keep the claim that fundamental dignity is not earned or extinguished, even by moral failure; attribute its foundation and resist turning other kinds of diminished dignity into diminished human worth.

Preserve gratitude for the historical identification of rights and the duty of international protection; rights are concrete expressions of intrinsic dignity, not merely a list of admired aspirations.
Keep the move from inalienable personal dignity to obligations toward society; contributing within one's ability protects participation without demanding identical capacity from everyone.
Retain the universal destination of both material and cultural goods; explain its creation-based grounding in foundations while preserving access and benefit beyond any one owner.

Keep the recognized right to private property and its subordination to the universal destination of goods; neither absolute ownership nor a claim that all property is denied is faithful to this doctrinal position.
Keep solidarity as recognition of interdependence turned into real responsibility and shared decisions; it requires more than an expression of sympathy.
Distinguish factual digital interconnection from deliberately chosen cooperation and mutual care; being connected does not by itself satisfy the virtue of solidarity.
Retain just conditions for everyone, especially the weakest, while placing following Jesus and Gospel fidelity in foundations; justice remains a structural demand rather than private benevolence.
Keep structural injustice, prevention and support for people still bearing past harms; correction after damage cannot replace fair structures or historical responsibility.

Keep migrants and refugees as the test of social justice, including safe legal routes and integration together with the right to remain safely at home; preserve displaced people's agency, resources and dreams rather than treating migration as one homogeneous problem.

Preserve all named forms of abuse, listening to victims, acknowledgment, reparation, prevention, shared resources and corrective assessment; the Church's religious mission must not screen its concrete duties from the secular main path.
Keep the transition from principles to technologies already affecting daily life; this signals application of the existing ethical framework rather than an unrelated AI-only document.

Preserve discernment as continuing rather than settled once for all, with people called to build humane relations together; keep Gospel motivation distinct from the practical need for renewed judgment.

Keep moral evil, possible conversion and Frankl's contrast between perpetrators and victims; the historical reference to prayer is not a prayer to remove, and hope must not excuse atrocity.
Preserve vulnerability as a possible opening to fraternity and art's resistance to normalized evil; keep the named works as interpretive examples, not evidence that all audiences react alike.

Retain concentrated communicative power, universal truth, conscience and sacred inviolable dignity. Arabic quotes arrogant self-creation and egoistic closure, but does not literally name original sin; do not import that wording from another edition.

Keep work's protected dignity and its capacity for shared achievement; Benedict's union of prayer and work is historical religious context, not a liturgical formula to delete.

Keep explicit delay, ecclesial slave ownership, regulatory legitimation, nineteenth-century formal absolute universal condemnation, eighteen centuries, contradiction, memory and institutional pardon; anti-anachronism does not cancel admitted complicity. Keep n175’s 1866 qualification.

Keep interreligious dialogue and the rejection of sanctified hatred, naming religious traditions as actors; this religious discussion is substantive peacebuilding rather than prayer to omit.

Preserve the Holy See's adoption of mercy as a diplomatic criterion and its concrete service to common-good peacebuilding; label the Gospel premise while avoiding a generic claim that diplomacy has no political consequences.

Keep the commitment to achieve peace in relationships and society and the attributed religious account of hope; exclude the repeated blessing and direct calls to pray, never the practical responsibility attached to them.

Retain the conclusion's careful-building and unity frame as the outline of a Christian program; separate prayer and ceremonial address from substantive common-good construction and contextual sacramental premises.

Keep the critique of disguised control of markets and influence alongside the religious alternative of mercy; the Magnificat functions as a theological interpretive frame, not evidence that the market diagnosis is scientifically established.

Keep attention to children, elderly people, victims and human struggle within the Incarnation argument; move its explicit theological grounding to foundations and remove the Lord's Prayer formula without losing vulnerable persons.

Keep the call to responsible participation and the human face at the center, with consciousness claims attributed; preserve recapitulation in Christ as an optional theological promise rather than secular technological prediction.

Preserve the Church's duty to share, oppose exclusion and give voice to invisible people; remove the opening liturgical response while keeping Eucharistic rationale in foundations rather than replacing it with secular individual piety.

Keep active responsibility, human limitations and the four closing commitments, with rejection of retreat into spiritual sentimentality; preserve the Kingdom and Christ imagery as attributed foundations.

Preserve relational creaturehood and responsibility for the whole creation. Arabic says المركزيّة البشريّة without a situated adjective; describe its following relational definition, without manufacturing a corrected exact quotation.

Keep patient adult formation, shared partnerships and young people's inner freedom; label evangelization as the Church's distinct vocation and do not turn the educational main path into a religious agreement test.

Retain physical presence, meals, care for lonely people and service to the poor amid digital connection; preserve the body's theological meaning without implying every digital relationship lacks authenticity.

Keep supply-chain examination, hidden work and business models profiting from manipulation or war alongside practical fairness and participation; separate Christ-grounded hope from the concrete ethical tasks.

Preserve the historical narrative of prayer, discernment before God and organized rebuilding, then the reader’s listening and courage, responsibility and concrete workplaces. Arabic says الإصغاء والشّجاعة; do not import Russian obedience terminology.

Preserve the explicit invitation to read history through sufferers, widows, orphans, strangers and displaced people; Marian framing goes to foundations, never into a whole-paragraph devotional omission that would erase these perspectives.

Keep sharing oneself and one's goods through everyday fidelity as the substantive closing task; exclude the final entrustment to Mary while preserving Incarnation and salvation-history claims as optional foundations rather than secular guarantees.

Keep promised productivity alongside possible deskilling, surveillance and lost agency; the criticism concerns current approaches and risks, not an assertion that automation always worsens every job.
Retain unemployment's serious consequences and State responsibility, with contraction fears limited to some contexts; do not present the passage as a quantitative forecast of global job losses.
Keep technological relief from arduous and dangerous tasks as desirable while preserving employment and the person as an end; the general protection rule is not an absolute ban on changing any job.
Preserve uneven transitions, different regional effects and the lack of a universal solution; adaptive local and national responses are central, not a footnote to a single global prescription.

Keep work's relational and civic roles, but also the duty to rethink citizenship where work diminishes so unemployment does not remove social participation; human worth must not become conditional on employment.

Retain organized responses from social teaching and the duty to prevent people being stranded among replacement machines; historical efforts are the basis for present institution-building rather than nostalgia for an unchanged labor market.
Keep anticipation of transformation, formation and dignified new work before jobs disappear; a purely reactive unemployment response loses the preventive agency of the passage.
Preserve economic activity's service to society and the creation of valuable jobs; business success is evaluated through its social contribution rather than exempted from responsibility.
Keep the contrast between proclaimed economic freedom and conditions preventing people from benefiting; promised automatic prosperity is criticized through its burdens on those with least power.

Retain critique of GDP-only development and the proposed complementary measures, work, shared prosperity, inequality, environment and peace through justice. The frozen sentence says تبين الأنشطة; do not silently repair it into an exact negative quotation.

Preserve the distinction between finance for productive development and speculative pursuits, including the discussion of cryptocurrencies; do not make every financial innovation synonymous with speculation.
Keep concentration of growing wealth and access to innovation's benefits, including care and knowledge; absolute aggregate growth alone does not answer distributive justice.
Retain redistributive laws and fair taxation while keeping justice throughout acquisition, financing, production and consumption; redistribution after production cannot absolve unjust processes.
Keep political responsibility beyond reliance on an invisible hand, with widespread inclusive sustainable prosperity; the passage does not propose that all market activity should cease.
Preserve the concrete economy-and-AI criteria that make innovation humane, especially accountable decisions and fair opportunities; their role is to civilize innovation rather than oppose it as such.

Preserve the source's definition of family as an enduring union of a man and a woman with explicit attribution, alongside its social-good claim; do not silently broaden that definition or present it as uncontested consensus.

Retain the family's fragility under changing work and the contrast between celebrated technical success and eroding social stability; this is an institutional effect, not blame placed on individual households.
Keep youth insecurity and the conditions for long-term commitments, with unpredictable economic risks; hope here requires more than encouragement to be confident.
Preserve the State's role in conditions for employment and protection during transition; supporting businesses is linked to people at the center rather than an unconditional benefit to firms.
Keep continuity/quality of work, the local trio العمل والخدمات والرّاحة, accessible formation/retraining and supportive social/educational networks. Do not substitute leisure for services.
Preserve dependencies, digital sobriety and protection of minors against exploitative models; distinguish responsibility for environments from treating vulnerable users as solely at fault.
Keep profiling and mass data collection as possible social control and the duty to safeguard conscience; the risk diagnosis is not a claim that every data use is surveillance.
Retain the criticism of treating a person as a manipulable object and its connection to tolerated subordination; freedom concerns a view of persons as well as the presence of technical controls.
Keep the digital economy's material and labor dependencies and the argument that efficiency cannot excuse subordination; no adaptation may describe digital products as immaterial or labor-free.
Retain new slavery as a decisive test of AI ethics and the warning about condemning old harms while tolerating new ones; advanced technology is not evidence of moral advancement.
Keep trafficking as grave violation and the insistence on firm response; do not reduce organized exploitation to unfortunate side effects of otherwise efficient markets.

Keep explicit delay, ecclesial slave ownership, regulatory legitimation, nineteenth-century formal absolute universal condemnation, eighteen centuries, contradiction, memory and institutional pardon; anti-anachronism does not cancel admitted complicity. Keep n175’s 1866 qualification.

Retain the move from admitted complicity to present prevention, protection, liberation and rehabilitation; religious responsibility motivates concrete action rather than replacing it with retrospective regret.

Keep the author's analysis of colonial data extraction, including health and genetic information, and people's power to decide use and benefit; returning copies of data alone would not meet the demand.

Preserve the distinct responsibilities of supply chains, investors, platforms, authorities and civil society; transparency, due diligence and victim protection must not collapse into a vague shared duty.
Keep the integration of truth, education, work, family and freedom into one development test; technical capacity requires a wise perspective to become growth, justice and fraternity.
Retain foresight, shared responsibilities and the inviolable dignity of every person as the measure of authentic progress; efficiency is not an independent exemption from that measure.
Preserve the chapter's turn to war as a test of moral maturity, particularly for governors; do not disperse responsibility so widely that those directing conflict disappear.
Keep cyberattacks, information and hybrid conflict alongside conventional warfare; the same social principles still guide decision-making across the changed forms of conflict.
Explain the contrast between domination and rebuilding through the prior biblical images; retain common-good construction as the substantive alternative and label the metaphors' religious origin.
Keep the diagnosis of polarization and violence together with civilization of love as an active construction site; hope is a program of work, not denial of the conflicts named.

Retain Paul VI's Cold War origin of civilization of love and the move from armed coexistence to a shared future; historical context prevents the phrase from becoming a slogan without institutional meaning.
Keep digital proximity as an opportunity requiring mutual care and rights and duties; network connection is not already a community with a shared future.
Preserve power's agenda-setting effects, weakening multilateralism and the claimed inevitability of force; that inevitability is the position criticized, not the author's conclusion.
Keep the historical call against war and the postwar effort to avoid another world war; distinguish the remembered aspiration from any claim that intervening conflicts did not occur.

Retain the source's diagnosis of normalization of war and rearmament in discourse, including algorithmic amplification of conflict; date and attribute this contemporary diagnosis instead of treating it as timeless data.
Keep the loss of witnesses to the Holocaust and World Wars and its implications for judgments by power alone; historical memory informs responsibility without substituting for present facts.
Preserve the contribution of fragmented communication to hostility and civilian suffering; avoid claiming one algorithm alone causes war or that communication is detached from material violence.
Keep financial and industrial interests that can fuel conflict in the author's diagnosis; do not infer an unproved motive for every individual involved in military production.
Retain concern about renewed arsenals and miniaturized weapons making use seem more viable; apparent usability does not reduce the destructive ethical stakes.

Keep weak diplomacy, complex interests and the asymmetry between starting and stopping war; preserve prevention as the neglected task rather than assuming every dispute has an immediate easy settlement.
Retain non-state armed groups and conflict sustained as a source of power or income; this complicates an account in which every conflict seeks a conventional final victory.

Preserve the Holy See's last-resort legitimate-self-defense condition and rigorous limits on AI weapons; do not turn the paragraph into either endorsement of autonomous violence or an unqualified claim that no force is ever permitted.

Keep the categorical non-delegation of lethal or irreversible decisions and the positive importance of values and prudent judgment in programming, moral ecology, conscience and model limits. Arabic has no as-far-as-possible qualification here; this is not machine moral agency.
Retain the three concrete criteria: traceable personal responsibility, time for moral judgment and protection of civilians; speed must not displace judgment in irreversible war decisions.
Keep reconstructable decision chains, effective self-aware human control and shared international safeguards; a nominal human button alone is not the control described by the author.
Preserve the crisis of institutions for a common future and mistrust among multiple powers; the passage criticizes conflict-ridden multipolarity rather than claiming one pole should dominate.
Keep enemy-based identity and narratives that bypass institutions, with consequences for cohesion; do not reproduce the good-versus-evil binary as the atlas's own categorization of peoples.
Preserve the displacement of development, disarmament and prevention, including civilian and child protection; describing those goods as naïve is the attitude being criticized.
Keep the costs of militarization borne by the poorest through reduced health, education and services; practical resource consequences must remain beside the critique of spiritual blindness.
Preserve the rejection of false realism and peace as the possible fruit of justice and charity; possibility is not a promise that every negotiation will succeed.
Retain the criticism of religious extremism and identity fanaticism alongside nihilistic pragmatism; religious language here carries self-critical moral analysis rather than a devotional formula.

Keep weakening moral limits, government interests rather than objective gravity, economic calculation, media illusions, frustrated promises and renewed violence as a warning, not a prediction of inevitability.
Preserve the open question of concrete safeguards and the critique of war used to divert domestic attention; identify the mechanism without inventing examples of named governments.
Keep researchers, businesses and institutions responsible for critical assessment of projects and their possible complicity; ignorance cannot automatically absolve participation in harmful systems.
Retain the naming of perpetual conflict as evil and the invitation to change its direction; distinguish Isaiah's theological hope from evidence that improvement is guaranteed.
Keep witnesses who persist in the darkest periods as grounds for the source's theological hope; preserve that religious account without converting it to a forecast of inevitable historical progress.
Keep everyday choices of truth, moderation and care as meaningful contributions, without claiming they alone solve large institutional conflicts; small agency coexists with public duties.

Use Tolkien's cited line as a literary illustration of responsibility within one's time, with the subsequent practical routes to peace; do not present a fictional character's words as empirical evidence.
Retain words' capacity to inflame or disarm, including denunciation of injustice and support for excluded voices; peaceful language must not mean silence about harm.

Preserve justice as the condition of true peace and concrete anti-theft/adultery/reciprocity examples. The Arabic question لماذا تريد أنت أن تتعارض مع العدل؟ is coherent; do not import Russian grammatical damage. Psalm 85,11 is not n084; Augustine is n191.

Retain the claim that neutrality can be unjust in some conflicts, with history and memory serving different roles; neither side-taking in every dispute nor erasing witnesses follows from the paragraph.
Keep victims' voices in communication and education as an appeal against evil and toward peace; recognizing suffering is not permission to cultivate revenge or new conflicts.

Preserve healthy realism's rejection of both purity that ignores conditions and cynicism that normalizes evil; verifiable guarantees, negotiation, prevention and civilian protection make the distinction practical.
Keep dialogue as the primary means of coexistence and the possibility of honorable solutions through perseverance; do not turn the claimed possibility into assurance of an easy settlement.
Retain ordinary listening to strangers and migrants as part of peacebuilding beyond State diplomacy; distinct everyday and political scales should remain intelligible.
Keep the political shift toward a culture of negotiation as a patient ethical and cultural commitment; diplomacy is a practice with time and institutions, not simply nicer speech.
Preserve the author's appeal to governors to reject a mindset dividing the world into the good and evil; attribution is essential when summarizing the quoted papal address.
Keep interreligious dialogue and the rejection of sanctified hatred, naming religious traditions as actors; this religious discussion is substantive peacebuilding rather than prayer to omit.
Preserve diplomacy's preventive and trust-building role, including attention to faint signs of goodwill; uncertainty and patience belong to the argument rather than a promised immediate result.

Keep cyberattacks, manipulation and AI-assisted influence as real violence requiring protection and international arrangements; invisibility does not make harms imaginary or exempt civilian interests.
Keep international institutions, dialogue, development, vulnerable people, disarmament and ecology with deep institutional reform and the ethical/value crisis; no merely technical repair.

Preserve the Holy See's adoption of mercy as a diplomatic criterion and its concrete service to common-good peacebuilding; label the Gospel premise while avoiding a generic claim that diplomacy has no political consequences.

Keep the commitment to achieve peace in relationships and society and the attributed religious account of hope; exclude the repeated blessing and direct calls to pray, never the practical responsibility attached to them.

Retain the conclusion's careful-building and unity frame as the outline of a Christian program; separate prayer and ceremonial address from substantive common-good construction and contextual sacramental premises.

Keep the critique of disguised control of markets and influence alongside the religious alternative of mercy; the Magnificat functions as a theological interpretive frame, not evidence that the market diagnosis is scientifically established.

Keep attention to children, elderly people, victims and human struggle within the Incarnation argument; move its explicit theological grounding to foundations and remove the Lord's Prayer formula without losing vulnerable persons.

Preserve the Incarnation's alternative to disembodied enhancement, including the acknowledged yearning for fuller life; exclude the devotional exclamation while retaining the doctrinal claim that divine love shares human fragility.

Keep the call to responsible participation and the human face at the center, with consciousness claims attributed; preserve recapitulation in Christ as an optional theological promise rather than secular technological prediction.

Keep Eucharistic communion as the stated origin of Christian solidarity; remove Augustine's recited response sequence while retaining his argument about membership and unity, not merely deleting the whole sacramental explanation.

Preserve the Church's duty to share, oppose exclusion and give voice to invisible people; remove the opening liturgical response while keeping Eucharistic rationale in foundations rather than replacing it with secular individual piety.

Keep active responsibility, human limitations and the four closing commitments, with rejection of retreat into spiritual sentimentality; preserve the Kingdom and Christ imagery as attributed foundations.

Preserve relational creaturehood and responsibility for the whole creation. Arabic says المركزيّة البشريّة without a situated adjective; describe its following relational definition, without manufacturing a corrected exact quotation.

Keep patient adult formation, shared partnerships and young people's inner freedom; label evangelization as the Church's distinct vocation and do not turn the educational main path into a religious agreement test.

Retain physical presence, meals, care for lonely people and service to the poor amid digital connection; preserve the body's theological meaning without implying every digital relationship lacks authenticity.

Keep supply-chain examination, hidden work and business models profiting from manipulation or war alongside practical fairness and participation; separate Christ-grounded hope from the concrete ethical tasks.

Preserve the historical narrative of prayer, discernment before God and organized rebuilding, then the reader’s listening and courage, responsibility and concrete workplaces. Arabic says الإصغاء والشّجاعة; do not import Russian obedience terminology.

Preserve Revelation's city as a promised gift with open gates and healing, and its call to overcome divisions; this eschatological image is not a secular infrastructure plan or an excuse to drop cooperation.

Keep the distinction between unchanged oppression and a changed perspective, and the claim that God sides with the lowly; remove the performed hymn of praise while retaining its theological and political interpretation in context.

Preserve the explicit invitation to read history through sufferers, widows, orphans, strangers and displaced people; Marian framing goes to foundations, never into a whole-paragraph devotional omission that would erase these perspectives.

Keep sharing oneself and one's goods through everyday fidelity as the substantive closing task; exclude the final entrustment to Mary while preserving Incarnation and salvation-history claims as optional foundations rather than secular guarantees.

publicCopyReview.scope: 762 explanation/label records; all headings, concept layers, 44 relationships, six finite trails and optional reflections.
publicCopyReview.method: Arabic wording follows the local edition’s terms. Public normative and anthropological claims remain attributed; source quotations and local note bodies remain exact. Fictional cases are visibly labelled and invent no named event, measurement or forecast.

groupReviews.review: Two building images, inherited generational responsibility, benefits and harms of technology, private power, dialogue, limits, shared work and practical planning; creation/Incarnation and biblical grounds attributed.

Dynamic teaching, earthly autonomy, distinct civil/ecclesial responsibilities, dialogue with sciences, local discernment, truth offered without coercion, and no single technical answer for all settings.

Distinct historical contributions, work and wages, social property, competition and collectivism criticism, democracy with participation, qualified markets, global inequality, ecology and continuity with changes in emphasis.
Principles considered together, Trinity/Incarnation/creation as grounds, four dignity meanings, practical universal rights, attributed life/abortion/euthanasia positions and women’s equal treatment.
Shared common good, public coordination, peoples’ rights, property’s social limit, digital goods, supported local agency, State duties, corporate power, chosen solidarity and future generations.

Structural/reparative justice, migrants’ agency and safe routes/right to remain, whole-person development, ecology, and Church transparency, real participation, abuse victims, reparation, prevention and resource sharing.

Present building choice, technocratic ends, real benefits, concentrated platform power, dated/limited AI account, effective computation versus attributed consciousness claims, impacts, recourse, prior participation and justice in design.

Performance reductionism, relational care, diverse enhancement currents, compulsory effort to remove suffering with finitude, integration of pain, moral evil/possible conversion, fragile institutions, witnesses and grace distinct from technical improvement.

Truth as shared good, verification and trust, communicative power, conscience, democracy, cultural formation, journalists and Church duty, patient education, supervised child protection, parents’ choice and educational access/pedagogy/knowledge.

Work beyond income without conditioning intrinsic worth, necessary emergency aid, desirable automation relief, contextual contraction risks, uneven national/local transitions, civic participation, unions, anticipatory formation and finance serving real work.

Unequal innovation access, justice throughout production, three §164 measures, attributed family definition, youth and services/rest, surveillance, hidden labor/extraction/trafficking, Church complicity and pardon, community power over data and concrete due diligence.

Hybrid/dual-use conflict, normalization and arms incentives, memory, strict legitimate defense and last resort, non-delegation, prudent values work, accountable chain, moral judgment time, civilians and actual conscious responsible human control.

Institutional weakness, distorted enemy identities, humanitarian safeguards, historical nihilism, false inevitability, researchers’ whole-system responsibilities and unequal but real everyday agency; hope inspires active resistance, not magic.

Disarmed words with denunciation of injustice, justice as peace’s condition, taking victims seriously, history/memory distinction, realistic change, dialogue, interreligious peace, diplomacy and deep institutional reform; unarmed/disarming/humble/persevering peace and practical commitment survive blessing removal.

Attributed Christian program, divine mercy/Incarnation and vulnerable people, transformed fragility, agency, Eucharistic solidarity and participation, active duties instead of spiritual retreat, truth, education, bodily presence, hidden work and fairness.

Nehemiah’s reported prayer and organization, listening/courage/responsibility, promised open city with present cooperation, changed perspective despite unchanged Roman domination, all six §244 vulnerable subjects, sharing, daily fidelity and attributed salvation history.

meaningChecks.p001: Keep the generational choice between humane and dehumanizing construction; put creation and Incarnation behind an attributed foundations link so the secular entry does not imply that these premises are universally accepted.

meaningChecks.p002: Preserve the Church's stated willingness to collaborate with all people in integral development; distinguish this inclusive invitation from its belief that divine action blesses those efforts.

meaningChecks.p003: Locate the present letter in the living social-teaching tradition inaugurated by Rerum Novarum; remove the closing invocation while keeping the argument that proclamation cannot ignore concrete social life.

meaningChecks.p004: Carry forward technology's possible benefits, harms and uncertain long-term effects; separate the appeal to ask God for wisdom from the practical need to interpret current transformations.

meaningChecks.p005: Keep regulation alongside the prior question of who controls technology; private transnational actors exceeding some governments' resources are part of the source's power analysis, not a reason to declare all private activity illegitimate.

meaningChecks.p006: Preserve shared discernment of ends rather than a succession of emergency responses; the open questions ask a community to choose a direction, not predict an inevitable technological future.

meaningChecks.p007: Use Babel as an explicitly biblical interpretation of uniformity and self-assertion, preserving the distinction between coordinated activity and homogenization; do not present the narrative as empirical evidence about AI.

meaningChecks.p008: Retain Nehemiah's listening, distributed work and shared responsibility as the narrative's argumentative work; keep his historical prayer in optional biblical context rather than misclassifying the reported action as a prayer addressed to the reader.

meaningChecks.p009: Preserve both technology's useful possibilities and its dependence on the choices of designers, funders, regulators and users; relocate the Holy Spirit and biblical construction frame without claiming a morally neutral tool.

meaningChecks.p010: Retain the critique of profit that sacrifices the weak and of reducing people to data; explain the two biblical paths as attributed metaphors while preserving plurality as a resource for community.

meaningChecks.p011: Keep the explicit argument that common-good building rests on relationship with God in optional foundations; exclude Augustine's direct prayer without converting the theological desire for fullness into an identical secular claim.

meaningChecks.p012: Keep vulnerability and limits as features of human life rather than failures to erase; progress is evaluated by everyone's dignity and peoples' good, not simply by increased technical capacity.

meaningChecks.p013: Retain shared responsibility, the strength-in-weakness biblical premise, differentiated contributors and cooperation between peoples, disciplines and cultures. Arabic does not explicitly name subsidiarity here; explain its cooperative logic without fabricating that term in a quotation.

meaningChecks.p014: Translate the demand for evangelical language into an attributed argument for truthful, non-humiliating communication; retain the institutional tasks of literacy, vulnerable-person protection and guiding research toward justice.

meaningChecks.p015: Use the appeal to remain human amid AI as orientation; keep Jubilee grace and humanity revealed in Christ as foundations rather than treating the ceremony as the source's main policy proposal.

meaningChecks.p016: Retain the call to plan, work and center people ordinarily excluded, while removing the direct prayer and implored blessing clauses; the common-good task must survive those exclusions.

meaningChecks.p017: Keep AI as a transformation questioning and developing the categories of social teaching from within, in fidelity to the Gospel; not a thematic appendix or isolated emergency.

meaningChecks.p018: Keep the Church's self-description as serving the common good and its distinct relationship to political communities; this explains the institutional speaker before presenting the sequence of popes.

meaningChecks.p019: Preserve the claim that religion cannot be relegated to private life and that the Church may comment on civil events; attribute that public-role claim rather than presenting it as an uncontested rule of politics.

meaningChecks.p020: Keep the acknowledgment of earthly realities' proper autonomy within the Church's theological account; do not erase either autonomy or the belief that the Spirit works within human endeavors.

meaningChecks.p021: Retain the distinction between ecclesiastical and civil responsibilities and the warning that exceptional Church substitutions cannot become normal; this limits institutional scope rather than licensing permanent replacement of public institutions.

meaningChecks.p022: Retain autonomy and distinct spheres, discerning contemporary voices with the Spirit and revealed truth, conversion and structural reform. Do not turn theological discernment into neutral sociology.

meaningChecks.p023: Retain the welcome offered to sincere seekers of truth, goodness and beauty, with scientific inquiry and diverse expert opinions; do not replace openness to debate with a claim that the Church settles empirical disputes.

meaningChecks.p024: Explain social teaching as discernment developed through Gospel and human knowledge, not a detached list of rules; its criteria concern persons, communities and the common good.

meaningChecks.p025: Keep truth as a shared gift and the warning against monopoly or prestige, including the polyhedron image for multiple perspectives; the source still claims one Gospel truth rather than relativism.

meaningChecks.p026: Preserve cultural and historical plurality in the Church's account of catholicity; local contexts matter to application, even while the text maintains a universal vocation.

meaningChecks.p027: Keep the contrast between a handbook and a living process of discernment, including dialogue, memory and prophecy; do not paraphrase the continuing presence of the Incarnate Word as merely institutional learning.

meaningChecks.p028: Retain the transition to selected stages since Rerum Novarum as a guide to the timeline; do not promise a comprehensive history beyond the overview the author supplies.

meaningChecks.p029: Preserve the distinction between ancient Gospel reception and its modern systematization; the source does not describe social doctrine as spontaneously invented in the modern age.

meaningChecks.p030: Keep Rerum Novarum's worker dignity, association and wage concerns as the historical starting point; preserve its claim that evangelization has structural consequences rather than replacing it with a purely economic origin story.

meaningChecks.p031: Keep criticism of unlimited competition and collectivist suppression of freedom/responsibility together with unions, wages, social property and opposition to racist totalitarianism.

meaningChecks.p032: Keep Pius XII's war-and-reconstruction context, law over force, intermediary organizations and international imbalances; this is an attributed historical account, not a claim that all those institutions worked as intended.

meaningChecks.p033: Preserve John XXIII's widening global focus and rights-based institutions and relations between peoples; do not reduce the development to a change of papal personnel.

meaningChecks.p034: Retain Vatican II's turning point, human dignity and pluralistic peaceful societies; the historical explanation must keep the concrete rights criteria rather than just celebratory Council language.

meaningChecks.p035: Keep Paul VI's account of peace as more than the absence of war, linked to humane development and poorer countries; do not treat economic growth alone as the definition of peace.

meaningChecks.p036: Preserve Octogesima Adveniens' engagement with postindustrial change and exclusion; the historical application requires that no person or people be treated as expendable.

meaningChecks.p037: Retain John Paul II's treatment of work amid ideological crisis, sufficient remuneration and participation; labor's personal dignity is more than its usefulness to production.

meaningChecks.p038: Keep underdevelopment, responsibility and solidarity in Sollicitudo Rei Socialis; preserve the connection to political charity and civilization of love as the source's normative frame.

meaningChecks.p039: Retain Centesimus Annus' reflection after the Soviet collapse together with continuing exploitation and representation crises; do not turn the passage into unconditional endorsement of whatever markets or democracies do.

meaningChecks.p040: Keep Benedict XVI's widening of development and the political community's irreplaceable responsibility; this limits a reading in which growth alone or private generosity supplies the common good.

meaningChecks.p041: Preserve charity joined to truth and its critical public role; the text does not define charity as private sentiment detached from institutions or justice.

meaningChecks.p042: Keep Francis' account of history through hopes and vulnerabilities and the Church's learning from the poor; the poor are participants in the institution's transformation, not merely recipients.

meaningChecks.p043: Retain integral ecology and the criticism of self-referential politics and finance in Laudato Si'; preserve the source's systemic connection between environmental and social harms.

meaningChecks.p044: Keep Fratelli Tutti's response to fragmentation, conflict and pandemic in the account of fraternity; its broad social friendship must not be narrowed to the author's own religious group.

meaningChecks.p045: Retain the conclusion that social teaching responds to concrete history while preserving an internal core; the overview invites attention to coherence, not a claim that no historical tensions exist.

meaningChecks.p046: Introduce the principles as interrelated within a living teaching in dialogue with history, cultures and sciences; individual concept cards must not imply that each principle stands alone.

meaningChecks.p047: Retain lay faithful and all people of good will applying principles in daily life, family, work and participation; academics and universities renewing them for digital change; theological/philosophical support for pastoral and teaching work.

meaningChecks.p048: Keep the Trinity as the stated source of received and shared love in optional foundations; it is a theological premise, not another name for interpersonal cooperation.

meaningChecks.p049: Preserve the Incarnation and Spirit-led life as the Christian grounding of social consequences; moving this explanation to foundations must not imply that the ethical claims had no religious basis.

meaningChecks.p050: Keep being created in God's image as the source's account of personhood and the person as the Church's way; retain that rationale separately from the secular statement of unconditional worth.

meaningChecks.p051: Retain worth before achievement, inalienable rights and arbitrary-power limits. The frozen final isolated word مليار has no developed argumentative referent; preserve it in source, disclose it rather than invent a billion-person claim.

meaningChecks.p052: Keep four locally named meanings separate: moral الكرامة الأخلاقيّة, social الكرامة الاجتماعيّة, experienced كرامة الحياة, intrinsic الكرامة الوجوديّة. The first three vary; no sin, failure, humiliation or exclusion removes the last, grounded here in divine willing, creation and love.

meaningChecks.p053: Keep the claim that fundamental dignity is not earned or extinguished, even by moral failure; attribute its foundation and resist turning other kinds of diminished dignity into diminished human worth.

meaningChecks.p054: Preserve gratitude for the historical identification of rights and the duty of international protection; rights are concrete expressions of intrinsic dignity, not merely a list of admired aspirations.

meaningChecks.p055: Keep universal rights and the source's explicit life-from-conception-to-natural-end position, including abortion and euthanasia, through clear Church attribution; secular navigation must not erase contested normative commitments.

meaningChecks.p056: Keep both dangers: rights declared only formally despite actual violations, and failure to sustain their universal foundation through inquiry; fearfully manipulated apparent consensus cannot establish legitimate protection.

meaningChecks.p057: Keep minority rights and women's equal dignity together with the continuing exclusions named by the author; a general equality slogan would lose the test of concrete treatment.

meaningChecks.p058: Preserve the priority of each person and family over grand ideological declarations; decent work, protections and necessities are the practical test of proclaimed dignity.

meaningChecks.p059: Keep the move from inalienable personal dignity to obligations toward society; contributing within one's ability protects participation without demanding identical capacity from everyone.

meaningChecks.p060: Use the Council's definition of social conditions enabling fulfillment for groups and individuals; retain the common good's moral dimension rather than presenting it as aggregate convenience.

meaningChecks.p061: Keep the whole's surplus over a sum of interests as an argument about shared life; do not turn the metaphor of a plus into a calculable metric or disregard individual persons.

meaningChecks.p062: Retain a people as a living reality formed through a shared vision and agreements; participation and differences remain part of that vision rather than enforced unanimity.

meaningChecks.p063: Keep State cohesion, unity, just coordination of interests and the weakest. The local warning is loss of long-term vision to short-term calculation or sterile polarization; add no corruption claim here.

meaningChecks.p064: Keep the international extension of the common good and rejection of eliminating or subjugating a nation; widening divisions are part of the source's diagnosis, not permission for domination.

meaningChecks.p065: Retain the universal destination of both material and cultural goods; explain its creation-based grounding in foundations while preserving access and benefit beyond any one owner.

meaningChecks.p066: Keep the recognized right to private property and its subordination to the universal destination of goods; neither absolute ownership nor a claim that all property is denied is faithful to this doctrinal position.

meaningChecks.p067: Extend the principle to patents, algorithms and platforms as the author does; preserve the environmental, waste and exploitation constraints instead of reducing the passage to open access alone.

meaningChecks.p068: Use the local descriptive term اللامركزيّة والتّكامل في اتّخاذ القرار; retain both non-absorption of lower bodies and active protection, coordination and support by higher institutions.

meaningChecks.p069: Preserve necessary State intervention and civil-society responsibility together; the paragraph explicitly rejects interpreting subsidiarity as State disengagement.

meaningChecks.p070: Keep decisions as close as possible to affected people and their meaningful involvement before choices are fixed; preserve support for intermediary associations rather than substituting individual consultation alone.

meaningChecks.p071: Apply subsidiarity to platform and corporate power, not only governments; independent checks, algorithm transparency, data access and recourse are concrete safeguards for meaningful participation.

meaningChecks.p072: Retain State and transnational safeguards that let varied communities help govern data and algorithms; local agency depends on wider cooperation rather than a handful of actors setting all rules.

meaningChecks.p073: Keep solidarity as recognition of interdependence turned into real responsibility and shared decisions; it requires more than an expression of sympathy.

meaningChecks.p074: Distinguish factual digital interconnection from deliberately chosen cooperation and mutual care; being connected does not by itself satisfy the virtue of solidarity.

meaningChecks.p075: Preserve solidarity as both institutional principle and personal virtue, including choices about consumption and technology that impede others' dignity; do not confine it to charitable feeling.

meaningChecks.p076: Keep global obligations and future generations within the assessment of technological decisions; benefits for an immediate minority cannot exhaust the evaluation.

meaningChecks.p077: Retain just conditions for everyone, especially the weakest, while placing following Jesus and Gospel fidelity in foundations; justice remains a structural demand rather than private benevolence.

meaningChecks.p078: Explain the preferential option for the poor through the groups the source names; preserve the priority of those most excluded without recasting it as a hierarchy of intrinsic human value.

meaningChecks.p079: Keep structural injustice, prevention and support for people still bearing past harms; correction after damage cannot replace fair structures or historical responsibility.

meaningChecks.p080: Apply social justice to networks, platforms and technological power; the passage asks that dignity and common good shape the digital environment rather than profit alone.

meaningChecks.p081: Keep migrants and refugees as the test of social justice, including safe legal routes and integration together with the right to remain safely at home; preserve displaced people's agency, resources and dreams rather than treating migration as one homogeneous problem.

meaningChecks.p082: Define development of all people and the whole person, all dimensions and future generations. Arabic n110 belongs here; import no English PDF/web note-boundary discrepancy.

meaningChecks.p083: Retain development as both right and duty with minimum enabling conditions, diverse peoples and ways of life; development is not imposed cultural uniformity.

meaningChecks.p084: Keep ecological responsibility, disadvantaged communities and those who follow us as inseparable conditions; technological gain cannot excuse degraded living conditions or environmental harm.

meaningChecks.p085: Use integral development as the evaluative frame for AI and robotics; the paragraph connects the preceding principles to later judgments instead of adding a separate technological ethic.

meaningChecks.p086: Preserve the Church's demand to apply its own principles internally, especially transparent decisions, accountable responsibilities and evaluation; keep the synodal mission as attributed institutional context rather than removing self-examination.

meaningChecks.p087: Retain real participation of the baptized and intermediary Church bodies, not nominal committees; name the ecclesial audience and the rejection of paternalism so this is not falsely generalized as an already achieved practice.

meaningChecks.p088: Keep sacramental communion as the Church's stated source of solidarity and diversity within unity; this is theological explanation without a direct prayer, not material to discard under the devotional rule.

meaningChecks.p089: Preserve all named forms of abuse, listening to victims, acknowledgment, reparation, prevention, shared resources and corrective assessment; the Church's religious mission must not screen its concrete duties from the secular main path.

meaningChecks.p090: Keep the transition from principles to technologies already affecting daily life; this signals application of the existing ethical framework rather than an unrelated AI-only document.

meaningChecks.p091: Preserve discernment as continuing rather than settled once for all, with people called to build humane relations together; keep Gospel motivation distinct from the practical need for renewed judgment.

meaningChecks.p092: Explain the technocratic paradigm as the reduction of nature and people to objects serving efficiency; retain its attribution to Francis and distinguish that critique from blanket rejection of tools.

meaningChecks.p093: Keep increased technical power alongside the failure to learn to use power well; the listed fields describe a convergence of capabilities, not evidence that each field inherently harms people.

meaningChecks.p094: Retain the warning that achievements can turn against humanity and that performance can become the chief measure of people; the source evaluates the direction of progress rather than opposing progress categorically.

meaningChecks.p095: Keep concentrated control over platforms and infrastructure as shaping dependence and exclusion; do not reduce structural power to an individual user's choice of good or bad use.

meaningChecks.p096: Retain the social principles as criteria for judging concentrated digital power; the ensuing account of AI must remain connected to that framework rather than stand as a technical encyclopedia.

meaningChecks.p097: Preserve the author's explicit limit on scope: this is neither a comprehensive AI treatment nor a literature survey; human conscience and freedom guide the discussion of uses and limits.

meaningChecks.p098: Keep rapid technical change and the dual need for scientific research and moral discernment; timestamp source claims rather than silently updating them or claiming technical finality.

meaningChecks.p099: Keep the author's distinctions between statistical adaptation, human experience and moral conscience, while labeling the categorical claims about AI's inner life as the source's position rather than settled scientific consensus.

meaningChecks.p100: Preserve both AI's value as a tool and vigilance about substituting simulated attention for relationships; the concern includes a possible loss of desire for human connection, not a claim that every interaction causes it.

meaningChecks.p101: Keep AI's cross-sector usefulness together with environmental costs and the call for lower-impact solutions; benefits must not erase material dependencies.

meaningChecks.p102: Retain effects on rights, opportunities and status and the danger of models reproducing designers' stereotypes; this frames deployment as a social judgment, not purely a technical optimization problem.

meaningChecks.p103: Preserve the critique of unaccountable algorithmic judgments about who is worthy and the disappearing political choices behind them; classification never removes the need for accountable human decisions.

meaningChecks.p104: Keep moral choices embedded in data, models and objectives before use; evaluating what a system was designed to do is necessary alongside evaluating a user's behavior.

meaningChecks.p105: Map responsibility throughout design, training, authorization and use, with reasons, monitoring, challenges and remedies; do not shorten accountability to a single final operator.

meaningChecks.p106: Keep prudence and sometimes slower adoption as responsible progress, supported by legal frameworks and independent oversight; generic ethical appeals are insufficient against infrastructure power.

meaningChecks.p107: Retain the distinction between aligning machines and debating the ends of society with affected communities; alignment does not settle who chooses values or remove people's ability to ask questions.

meaningChecks.p108: Keep shared governance of data, non-passive intermediate bodies and communities, access and justice. Arabic specifically says جماعات المؤمنين; do not silently replace that local attribution with an invented universal quotation.

meaningChecks.p109: Apply the principles to data and computational power with justice built into design; later repair remains important but cannot substitute for fair initial structures.

meaningChecks.p110: Explain disarming AI as freeing it from an adversarial mentality and making it accessible and welcoming; retain the author's argument that regulation alone is insufficient, without mistaking the metaphor for a technical weapon-removal procedure.

meaningChecks.p111: Preserve design as possible participation in creation, embedded values, transparency and responsibility; Arabic names الجماعات المسيحيّة المعنيّة, which must remain an attributed local premise rather than an unmarked universal source quote.

meaningChecks.p112: Retain the question of safeguarding humanity when people see themselves as optimization projects; relationship and communion limit performance-based pictures of the person.

meaningChecks.p113: Keep the warning against absolutizing any single human dimension, including intelligence; the claimed disorder can arise from disproportionate excess as well as scarcity.

meaningChecks.p114: Preserve civilization's test of care and the person as a subject of relationships and decisions; technical assistance can serve care without replacing responsible human presence.

meaningChecks.p115: Introduce the cultural narratives of enhancement and human-machine hybridity before their evaluation; label this as the author's framing of a debate rather than an exhaustive taxonomy.

meaningChecks.p116: Keep the plurality of transhumanist and posthumanist currents, the qualification about more radical forms and their often speculative status; do not attribute a single extreme program to everyone using either term.

meaningChecks.p117: Preserve the distinction between human-centered use of technology and a vision that devalues limits or ranks lives by usefulness; criticism targets the guiding outlook rather than all technological assistance.

meaningChecks.p118: Arabic explicitly says يجب علينا أن نسعى إلى إزالة الألم: preserve the obligation to strive to remove suffering alongside wisely recognizing intrinsic finitude and the faith-based interpretation of contingency. No refusal of treatment or romanticization of harm follows.

meaningChecks.p119: Keep compassion and the possibility of wisdom and closeness amid loss and failure; divine presence and worship are the source's additional religious interpretation, not a guarantee that suffering improves everyone.

meaningChecks.p120: Retain the attributed philosophical argument about integrating pain, love, desire, scars, freedom and failure, alongside §118’s obligation to strive to remove suffering. Do not make a clinical prescription.

meaningChecks.p121: Keep moral evil, possible conversion and Frankl's contrast between perpetrators and victims; the historical reference to prayer is not a prayer to remove, and hope must not excuse atrocity.

meaningChecks.p122: Preserve vulnerability as a possible opening to fraternity and art's resistance to normalized evil; keep the named works as interpretive examples, not evidence that all audiences react alike.

meaningChecks.p123: Retain history's institutional achievements in protecting people as well as its violence; present their fragility and the responsibility to sustain them rather than inevitable moral improvement.

meaningChecks.p124: Keep particular movements and witnesses of human dignity as examples of change; the selected figures illustrate the source's claim and are not a complete or uniform account of world history.

meaningChecks.p125: Preserve hidden service and perseverance alongside public witnesses, with religious communities and named believers as actual examples; do not turn credible witness into a purely technological mechanism of progress.

meaningChecks.p126: Keep the welcome for progress that relieves suffering on condition it preserves relationship and love; distinguish this practical condition from the Christian answer locating fulfillment in grace.

meaningChecks.p127: Keep the account of self-transcendence through divine gift and the Spirit, including Aquinas' disparity between created nature and divine life; secular self-improvement is not an equivalent paraphrase of grace.

meaningChecks.p128: Keep grace and communion as theological premises while retaining the contrast between algorithmic correction and a person's possible transformation through error; the person's future is not to be treated as exhausted by a prediction.

meaningChecks.p129: Preserve Christian humanism's welcome for science under common-good and care criteria, with both conditional outcomes of technological progress; neither automatic optimism nor blanket fear represents the text.

meaningChecks.p130: Use Augustine's two loves as an attributed moral interpretation of personal and institutional priorities; preserve the inward challenge without confusing two cities with a geographic or partisan division.

meaningChecks.p131: Keep the three announced application areas together: truth in public life, work's dignity and freedom from dependence and commercialization; the chapter is broader than employment alone.

meaningChecks.p132: Preserve the double potential of platforms and AI for dialogue and manipulation; factual veracity is proposed as a common good necessary to just communication.

meaningChecks.p133: Retain concentrated communicative power, universal truth, conscience and sacred inviolable dignity. Arabic quotes arrogant self-creation and egoistic closure, but does not literally name original sin; do not import that wording from another edition.

meaningChecks.p134: Retain truth's enabling role in democracy and the warning about losing distinctions between fact and fiction; do not convert this into a demand that everyone share a political opinion.

meaningChecks.p135: Keep communication as cultural formation rather than information transfer alone; the online world affects lived relationships and imagination, especially among young people.

meaningChecks.p136: Preserve platform power over collective imagination and the positive goal of inner freedom and critical thought; a communication environment can nurture rather than dominate readers.

meaningChecks.p137: Keep the refusal both to demonize and idolize tools, joined to verification and understanding complexity; responsible use requires intellectual formation beyond a checklist of apps.

meaningChecks.p138: Preserve journalists' role in exposing Church abuse and the institution's duty to confront uncomfortable facts without external compulsion; do not sanitize the source's shame or transfer responsibility to reporters.

meaningChecks.p139: Keep education's importance amid manipulation and the fatigue that discourages seeking truth; distinguish the diagnosed pressures from an assertion that young people are inherently incapable of thought.

meaningChecks.p140: Preserve patient engagement with reality and the warning that convenient AI answers can make thinking seem unnecessary; do not state that every use of AI blocks learning.

meaningChecks.p141: Retain the source's concerns about early unsupervised exposure, bullying and sensitive images with source date and attribution; its appeal to literature is not a substitute for current clinical guidance or a universal diagnosis.

meaningChecks.p142: Keep parents' limited ability to resist attention markets and the need for shared safeguards and literacy; assigning the whole duty to families would change the passage's institutional agency.

meaningChecks.p143: Retain parents’ primary and inalienable right to choose education and formation according to moral, cultural and religious convictions, alongside truth, relationships and critical thought.

meaningChecks.p144: Retain inequalities in educational access and the duty to make schooling accessible regardless of family resources; the socio-political challenge must remain visible beside pedagogical concerns.

meaningChecks.p145: Keep the pedagogical challenge of integral formation and critical, creative use of technology; catching up with devices is not the same as educating a person.

meaningChecks.p146: Preserve intellectual discipline, reading and careful analysis as conditions for inner freedom; do not promise an effortless atlas that replaces the intellectual work the text values.

meaningChecks.p147: Keep the shared educational alliance among families, schools, Christian communities and public institutions; retain time and trustworthy relationships as things technology alone cannot supply.

meaningChecks.p148: Keep work's protected dignity and its capacity for shared achievement; Benedict's union of prayer and work is historical religious context, not a liturgical formula to delete.

meaningChecks.p149: Preserve work's personal value and the allowance for emergency financial assistance; the limitation concerns aid as the sole response, not condemnation of every form of income support.

meaningChecks.p150: Keep promised productivity alongside possible deskilling, surveillance and lost agency; the criticism concerns current approaches and risks, not an assertion that automation always worsens every job.

meaningChecks.p151: Retain unemployment's serious consequences and State responsibility, with contraction fears limited to some contexts; do not present the passage as a quantitative forecast of global job losses.

meaningChecks.p152: Keep technological relief from arduous and dangerous tasks as desirable while preserving employment and the person as an end; the general protection rule is not an absolute ban on changing any job.

meaningChecks.p153: Preserve uneven transitions, different regional effects and the lack of a universal solution; adaptive local and national responses are central, not a footnote to a single global prescription.

meaningChecks.p154: Keep work's relational and civic roles, but also the duty to rethink citizenship where work diminishes so unemployment does not remove social participation; human worth must not become conditional on employment.

meaningChecks.p155: Retain organized responses from social teaching and the duty to prevent people being stranded among replacement machines; historical efforts are the basis for present institution-building rather than nostalgia for an unchanged labor market.

meaningChecks.p156: Keep anticipation of transformation, formation and dignified new work before jobs disappear; a purely reactive unemployment response loses the preventive agency of the passage.

meaningChecks.p157: Preserve economic activity's service to society and the creation of valuable jobs; business success is evaluated through its social contribution rather than exempted from responsibility.

meaningChecks.p158: Keep the contrast between proclaimed economic freedom and conditions preventing people from benefiting; promised automatic prosperity is criticized through its burdens on those with least power.

meaningChecks.p159: Retain critique of GDP-only development and the proposed complementary measures, work, shared prosperity, inequality, environment and peace through justice. The frozen sentence says تبين الأنشطة; do not silently repair it into an exact negative quotation.

meaningChecks.p160: Preserve the distinction between finance for productive development and speculative pursuits, including the discussion of cryptocurrencies; do not make every financial innovation synonymous with speculation.

meaningChecks.p161: Keep concentration of growing wealth and access to innovation's benefits, including care and knowledge; absolute aggregate growth alone does not answer distributive justice.

meaningChecks.p162: Retain redistributive laws and fair taxation while keeping justice throughout acquisition, financing, production and consumption; redistribution after production cannot absolve unjust processes.

meaningChecks.p163: Keep political responsibility beyond reliance on an invisible hand, with widespread inclusive sustainable prosperity; the passage does not propose that all market activity should cease.

meaningChecks.p164: Preserve the concrete economy-and-AI criteria that make innovation humane, especially accountable decisions and fair opportunities; their role is to civilize innovation rather than oppose it as such.

meaningChecks.p165: Preserve the source's definition of family as an enduring union of a man and a woman with explicit attribution, alongside its social-good claim; do not silently broaden that definition or present it as uncontested consensus.

meaningChecks.p166: Retain the family's fragility under changing work and the contrast between celebrated technical success and eroding social stability; this is an institutional effect, not blame placed on individual households.

meaningChecks.p167: Keep youth insecurity and the conditions for long-term commitments, with unpredictable economic risks; hope here requires more than encouragement to be confident.

meaningChecks.p168: Preserve the State's role in conditions for employment and protection during transition; supporting businesses is linked to people at the center rather than an unconditional benefit to firms.

meaningChecks.p169: Keep continuity/quality of work, the local trio العمل والخدمات والرّاحة, accessible formation/retraining and supportive social/educational networks. Do not substitute leisure for services.

meaningChecks.p170: Preserve dependencies, digital sobriety and protection of minors against exploitative models; distinguish responsibility for environments from treating vulnerable users as solely at fault.

meaningChecks.p171: Keep profiling and mass data collection as possible social control and the duty to safeguard conscience; the risk diagnosis is not a claim that every data use is surveillance.

meaningChecks.p172: Retain the criticism of treating a person as a manipulable object and its connection to tolerated subordination; freedom concerns a view of persons as well as the presence of technical controls.

meaningChecks.p173: Keep the digital economy's material and labor dependencies and the argument that efficiency cannot excuse subordination; no adaptation may describe digital products as immaterial or labor-free.

meaningChecks.p174: Retain new slavery as a decisive test of AI ethics and the warning about condemning old harms while tolerating new ones; advanced technology is not evidence of moral advancement.

meaningChecks.p175: Keep trafficking as grave violation and the insistence on firm response; do not reduce organized exploitation to unfortunate side effects of otherwise efficient markets.

meaningChecks.p176: Keep explicit delay, ecclesial slave ownership, regulatory legitimation, nineteenth-century formal absolute universal condemnation, eighteen centuries, contradiction, memory and institutional pardon; anti-anachronism does not cancel admitted complicity. Keep n175’s 1866 qualification.

meaningChecks.p177: Retain the move from admitted complicity to present prevention, protection, liberation and rehabilitation; religious responsibility motivates concrete action rather than replacing it with retrospective regret.

meaningChecks.p178: Keep the author's analysis of colonial data extraction, including health and genetic information, and people's power to decide use and benefit; returning copies of data alone would not meet the demand.

meaningChecks.p179: Preserve the distinct responsibilities of supply chains, investors, platforms, authorities and civil society; transparency, due diligence and victim protection must not collapse into a vague shared duty.

meaningChecks.p180: Keep the integration of truth, education, work, family and freedom into one development test; technical capacity requires a wise perspective to become growth, justice and fraternity.

meaningChecks.p181: Retain foresight, shared responsibilities and the inviolable dignity of every person as the measure of authentic progress; efficiency is not an independent exemption from that measure.

meaningChecks.p182: Preserve the chapter's turn to war as a test of moral maturity, particularly for governors; do not disperse responsibility so widely that those directing conflict disappear.

meaningChecks.p183: Keep cyberattacks, information and hybrid conflict alongside conventional warfare; the same social principles still guide decision-making across the changed forms of conflict.

meaningChecks.p184: Explain the contrast between domination and rebuilding through the prior biblical images; retain common-good construction as the substantive alternative and label the metaphors' religious origin.

meaningChecks.p185: Keep the diagnosis of polarization and violence together with civilization of love as an active construction site; hope is a program of work, not denial of the conflicts named.

meaningChecks.p186: Retain Paul VI's Cold War origin of civilization of love and the move from armed coexistence to a shared future; historical context prevents the phrase from becoming a slogan without institutional meaning.

meaningChecks.p187: Keep digital proximity as an opportunity requiring mutual care and rights and duties; network connection is not already a community with a shared future.

meaningChecks.p188: Preserve power's agenda-setting effects, weakening multilateralism and the claimed inevitability of force; that inevitability is the position criticized, not the author's conclusion.

meaningChecks.p189: Keep the historical call against war and the postwar effort to avoid another world war; distinguish the remembered aspiration from any claim that intervening conflicts did not occur.

meaningChecks.p190: Retain the source's diagnosis of normalization of war and rearmament in discourse, including algorithmic amplification of conflict; date and attribute this contemporary diagnosis instead of treating it as timeless data.

meaningChecks.p191: Keep the loss of witnesses to the Holocaust and World Wars and its implications for judgments by power alone; historical memory informs responsibility without substituting for present facts.

meaningChecks.p192: Preserve the contribution of fragmented communication to hostility and civilian suffering; avoid claiming one algorithm alone causes war or that communication is detached from material violence.

meaningChecks.p193: Keep financial and industrial interests that can fuel conflict in the author's diagnosis; do not infer an unproved motive for every individual involved in military production.

meaningChecks.p194: Retain concern about renewed arsenals and miniaturized weapons making use seem more viable; apparent usability does not reduce the destructive ethical stakes.

meaningChecks.p195: Keep weak diplomacy, complex interests and the asymmetry between starting and stopping war; preserve prevention as the neglected task rather than assuming every dispute has an immediate easy settlement.

meaningChecks.p196: Retain non-state armed groups and conflict sustained as a source of power or income; this complicates an account in which every conflict seeks a conventional final victory.

meaningChecks.p197: Preserve the Holy See's last-resort legitimate-self-defense condition and rigorous limits on AI weapons; do not turn the paragraph into either endorsement of autonomous violence or an unqualified claim that no force is ever permitted.

meaningChecks.p198: Keep the categorical non-delegation of lethal or irreversible decisions and the positive importance of values and prudent judgment in programming, moral ecology, conscience and model limits. Arabic has no as-far-as-possible qualification here; this is not machine moral agency.

meaningChecks.p199: Retain the three concrete criteria: traceable personal responsibility, time for moral judgment and protection of civilians; speed must not displace judgment in irreversible war decisions.

meaningChecks.p200: Keep reconstructable decision chains, effective self-aware human control and shared international safeguards; a nominal human button alone is not the control described by the author.

meaningChecks.p201: Preserve the crisis of institutions for a common future and mistrust among multiple powers; the passage criticizes conflict-ridden multipolarity rather than claiming one pole should dominate.

meaningChecks.p202: Keep enemy-based identity and narratives that bypass institutions, with consequences for cohesion; do not reproduce the good-versus-evil binary as the atlas's own categorization of peoples.

meaningChecks.p203: Preserve the displacement of development, disarmament and prevention, including civilian and child protection; describing those goods as naïve is the attitude being criticized.

meaningChecks.p204: Keep the costs of militarization borne by the poorest through reduced health, education and services; practical resource consequences must remain beside the critique of spiritual blindness.

meaningChecks.p205: Preserve the rejection of false realism and peace as the possible fruit of justice and charity; possibility is not a promise that every negotiation will succeed.

meaningChecks.p206: Retain the criticism of religious extremism and identity fanaticism alongside nihilistic pragmatism; religious language here carries self-critical moral analysis rather than a devotional formula.
